products.note: Open-weight MoE; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
DeepSeek AI, founded in 2023 and headquartered in Hangzhou, open-sources frontier large language models including mixture-of-experts architectures, making frontier AI capabilities available without licensing restrictions.

The company's strategy of releasing open-weight models as frontier products differs sharply from the closed-model approach of larger Western labs. DeepSeek-V4-Pro includes agent capabilities and API access, meaning the weights and architecture are public while the company provides inference infrastructure. This distribution model affects compute economics: users can run these models on their own infrastructure or pay for DeepSeek's inference, reducing dependence on any single provider's compute.

For AI scaling constrained by power and buildings, open-weight models shift where compute must be provisioned. If frontier models are open-source, incremental demand for inference can be served by distributed inference rather than concentrated data center capacity. This matters because it decouples frontier model capability from any single entity's power budget. The data does not cover DeepSeek's own infrastructure scale, training compute, or power consumption, so the net effect on total grid demand remains unclear.

The record contains no litigation, patents, or SEC filings for DeepSeek AI, limiting visibility into how the company protects its methods or plans capital deployment. The note flagging cross-border data review reflects that the company is Chinese-headquartered, which affects data residency and regulatory risk for users, though these concerns sit outside compute and power constraints.

profile_text.body:
DeepSeek AI, founded in 2023 and headquartered in Hangzhou, describes itself as focused on researching foundational artificial intelligence models and technology. The company states it is open-sourcing frontier large models including DeepSeek-V4 and DeepSeek-R1, and offers conversational access to DeepSeek AI alongside API integration.

The company's primary product is DeepSeek, an open-weight mixture-of-experts model available through its website. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is the latest release, which the company describes as offering improved text and agent performance alongside native multimodal vision understanding capabilities, with claimed improvements in capability, speed, and cost efficiency.
